topic.definition: A worked example is a small piece of real, running code that shows one idea doing its job. It is kept beside the idea rather than in a separate collection, so that a reader who has just been told what something is can see it work without going looking.
topic.do_not_use_when: Do not use one as the definition. An example shows one case; the definition has to cover the ones nobody wrote an example for.
topic.purpose: An example that is run by the same machinery that runs everything else cannot quietly stop being true, which is what makes it worth more than a snippet somebody pasted into a page.
topic.summary: A small, runnable illustration of an idea, kept beside the idea itself.
topic.use_when: Reach for a worked example when an idea is easier to recognize than to describe.
